evidence.summary: Header comment and ACCOUNTS map: accounts are keyed by (provider, subject); the provider sends email and email_verified.
callback() creates an account the first time a (provider, subject) pair is seen, with id 'lu-<n>', the provider's email and role 'member', and returns it; email_verified is accepted but never used.
callback() returns the account record and issues no session or token; the email stored is the one from the first sign-in and is never updated.

architecture.backend: single Python module with module-level state

features.name: Sign in with an OAuth provider
features.description: Sign in through an external identity provider; an account is created on first sign-in.
features.observed_behaviour: The callback receives provider, subject, email and email_verified; it finds or creates the account for (provider, subject) and returns it.
features.business_logic: Identity key is (provider, subject), not email. New accounts get role 'member'. email_verified is ignored. No link to password accounts.
features.integration: Needs the unified user store, an account-linking rule and the unified session mechanism.

auth.model: one role string per account, no permission checks in this app

error_handling.behaviour: no validation and no errors raised in callback()

unknowns: The OAuth flow before the callback (redirect, state/nonce, code exchange, ID-token signature and audience checks) is not in the provided code; how Linkup verifies the provider's response is unknown. The rest of the Linkup repository would settle it.
Linkup's session mechanism after sign-in is unknown: callback() returns the account and issues no token.
The task says Linkup is MIT, but sources/linkup has no LICENSE file; code_reuse is recorded as not-allowed until a licence file is provided.
